speaker: (a woman at the sacks)
text: Who is buying the barley, and is it for bread or for the steep?

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Let her ask. The new wheat is six-and-thirty the quarter, and that is loud enough without me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six-and-thirty. I am not buying it.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Butter, a little cheese, and the eggs. We are a glove stall. We are not the corn.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The gloves are behind me. You may look. You may not describe a seam.

speaker: (a woman at the sacks)
text: Six-and-thirty, and the barley already spoken for. A sack is a loaf if it is let stay a sack.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have paid none for barley. That was last night's answer, and it is still none.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The corn-sellers are few, and attended like physicians. I am a glover. I am not their clerk.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: He can stand off the board and still have heard six-and-thirty.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: None does not sell a glove. Stand off the board.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The rushes for the house are already in. I am not opening a purse at the Cross to make a speech of them.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The children want the north end. If the ladder will have me, I am going up it. The stall is Richard's, and Joan can sell.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: I can sell. Go and be advice on a rung, if the rung wants you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll go with the children. The row is the one they kept from Sunday.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Go. You are not a second clerk for the sacks. Bring them back by the bakehouse. I am not losing three children in a row of ash.

speaker: (a woman at the sacks)
text: If any man at this Cross is buying barley for mouths, he should say so where the sacks can hear.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: She can say it, and she is saying it. I am for the ladder when the stall can spare me.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Remembering a wheelwright will not sell a glove. The board is mine. The north end is yours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am aside. Six-and-thirty is heard. None is still the answer.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The eggs will not become a speech. Take the children before they take you.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thursday is the row, as they asked. Do not make it a second market.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The stall first, until I am actually on the ladder. You will hear me when I am.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will hear you. I am not describing a seam on the way.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Then the seam is safe. Go north when the board can spare you.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The board can spare him. It could have spared him at the first egg.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bakehouse after the row. I have not promised a shop, and I am not starting one at a stall.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Off, then. Six-and-thirty can shout without a glover to help it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: I will be at the bakehouse with the basket. Do not let Judith feed them before I see them.
